title: The hosted check in CI
body:
## Summary

A pull request that changes what the hosted images are built from can no longer merge unless the hosted check passes: CI builds every image on GitHub's runner, starts a throwaway copy with `infra/hosted/check.sh`, and runs its cases, the acceptance suite and the backup round trip against it. Source code alone does not trigger it, so most pull requests do not pay the build.

Best read in this order:

1. `scripts/ci/changed-areas.sh`: a ninth output line, `hosted=true|false`, the new concept of this slice. It is true for `infra/hosted/`, `scripts/deploy/`, `infra/postgres/`, `.github/workflows/`, `infra/services.json`, any `Dockerfile` or `.dockerignore`, and any dependency manifest, lockfile or toolchain pin by file name, wherever it is; and with `--all`.
2. `scripts/ci/dockerfile.sh`: the Dockerfile lock rules, moved unchanged out of `infra/hosted/tests/agree.test.sh` so that `agree.test.sh` and `scripts/ci/workflows-locked.test.sh` share one copy. `workflows-locked.test.sh` now holds every tracked Dockerfile to them, in CI's `scripts` job on every pull request.
3. `.github/workflows/hosted.yml`: the reusable workflow. It points `platform.test` at the runner, installs uv, Chromium and `design/ui`'s packages, runs `check.sh`, and uploads the compose logs on failure.
4. `.github/workflows/ci.yml`: the `hosted` output and job, and `ci-ok` needing it. `scripts/ci/ci-ok.test.sh` now also checks that `ci-ok` needs every other job in `ci.yml`.
5. `infra/hosted/check.sh`: with `HOSTED_CHECK_LOGS` set, a run with a failed case writes `docker compose ps -a` and `docker compose logs` there before the teardown, proved by a new case, `it_saves_the_logs_of_a_failed_run`.
6. Step 9 of `.claude/skills/pick-up-slice/SKILL.md` and the docs Settled names.

Closes #260

## Tasks

- [x] Add the `hosted` output to `scripts/ci/changed-areas.sh`, with its tests, and the Dockerfile rule to `workflows-locked.test.sh`: f260499
- [x] Add `.github/workflows/hosted.yml`, the `hosted` job in `ci.yml`, and `ci-ok` needing it: 4d13a17
- [x] Teach step 9 of `.claude/skills/pick-up-slice/SKILL.md` the hosted check, and change the docs named in Settled: 681a250

## Decisions the agent made

- **owner-decision.** `hosted.yml` installs Node 26 and runs `npm ci` in `design/ui/`, though Settled says the job "installs no Rust, Node or .NET". Alternative: Node left out, as Settled says. Why: the acceptance suite `check.sh` runs injects `design/ui/node_modules/axe-core/axe.min.js` from the checkout into the gallery, the nav bar and the memory centre (`e2e/tests/test_style.py:19`, and "Running it" in `e2e/README.md`). On a fresh runner that file does not exist, so those tests fail, and Acceptance requires `check.sh` to exit zero there. Only `design/ui`'s packages are installed, nothing is built, since every page is served from the images. Node 26 by `actions/setup-node` at the commit `e2e.yml` and `web.yml` pin, rather than the runner's preinstalled Node, so the install runs on the Node `.node-version` names. This goes against Settled, case 1 of step 8, hence `has-decision`.
- Every action in `hosted.yml` is pinned to a commit with its version in a comment, `actions/checkout` (v7.0.1) and `actions/upload-artifact` (v7.0.2) included. Alternative: `actions/checkout@v7` and `actions/upload-artifact@v7` by tag, as every other workflow references GitHub's own actions. Why: Settled asks for commit pins; its "as in the other workflows" holds only for the third party actions there. The stricter option on supply chain, and the SHAs were read with `gh api repos/<action>/git/ref/tags/<tag>`.
- The Dockerfile lock rules moved into `scripts/ci/dockerfile.sh` (`commands` and `unlocked`), called by both `agree.test.sh` and `workflows-locked.test.sh`. Alternative: a second copy of the awk in `workflows-locked.test.sh`. Why: two copies of a rule drift, and then one test passes what the other refuses. `agree.test.sh`'s own broken copy cases, all of which still pass, check the shared rules from its side.
- `workflows-locked.test.sh` finds Dockerfiles with `git ls-files ':(glob)**/Dockerfile'` and expects 9 installs among them, as its other checks expect counts, so an install moved out of the check's reach fails it. Alternative: `find`, which would also see untracked build output.
- `ci-ok.test.sh` gained a check that `ci-ok`'s `needs` lists every other job in `ci.yml`. Alternative: only the two Acceptance cases, which pass against today's `ci-ok.sh` unchanged, since it is generic. Why: the real risk is a job left out of `needs`, which would let it fail and still merge; this is the test that went red before `hosted` was added.
- `check.sh` saves `docker compose ps -a` beside the logs, and a new case, `it_saves_the_logs_of_a_failed_run`, proves the saving on the run it already makes fail once Postgres is up. Alternative: the logs alone, unchecked. Why: the containers' exit codes are what a failed CI run is read by first, and an untested log path is found broken on the day it is needed.
- `hosted=true|false` is printed last, after `dotnet_services`, as Settled's "ninth line" reads. `hosted.yml` has `workflow_call` alone, as Settled says, with no `workflow_dispatch`: a manual run of `ci.yml` runs `--all`, which sets `hosted`.
- The file name rules match anywhere in the tree, so `e2e/pyproject.toml` or `libs/python/platform-auth/pyproject.toml` set `hosted` too. Settled says "of any service, library or frontend"; the suite and the library are both read by `check.sh` or copied into an image, so matching by name is the simpler rule and errs towards running the check.
- Step 9's new entry also says to install Chromium and `design/ui`'s packages first when the e2e step did not run, since `hosted=true` without `e2e=true` happens, for a change to `.dockerignore` or `scripts/deploy/` alone.

## Verification

Gate, for the areas `changed-areas.sh` printed as true (`core=true canary=true brain=true libs=true scripts=true web=true e2e=true dotnet_services=[review] hosted=true`, every area since a workflow changed), on the Mac mini at 681a250:

- core: `cargo fmt --check` passed; `services.sh run core migrate` passed; `cargo clippy --locked --all-targets -- -D warnings` passed; `cargo test --locked` passed, every suite `ok`; `cargo test --locked --test app_roles -- --ignored` 3 passed; `cargo sqlx prepare --check -- --all-targets --locked` (sqlx-cli 0.9.0) passed.
- canary: `ruff check`, `ruff format --check` passed; `pytest` 21 passed.
- brain: `ruff check`, `ruff format --check`, `mypy` passed; migrate passed; `pytest` 401 passed.
- libs: `libs/python/platform-auth` ruff, format, mypy passed, `pytest` 64 passed; `libs/dotnet/PlatformAuth` restore `--locked-mode`, `dotnet format --verify-no-changes`, build and test passed, 44 passed.
- dotnet (review): restore `--locked-mode`, format, Release build, migrate, `dotnet test` 201 passed.
- scripts: every `scripts/**/*.test.sh` passed (18 files), among them `changed-areas.test.sh` 102 passed, `ci-ok.test.sh` 12 passed, `workflows-locked.test.sh` 13 passed.
- web: `design/ui` 198, `Brain/web` 113, `review/web` 125 vitest tests passed; `npm ci`, `biome ci`, `tsc --noEmit` and `npm run build` passed in each.
- e2e: platform started from the branch, every health path 200; `uv run pytest` 275 passed, 4 deselected; `ruff check` and `ruff format --check` passed.
- hosted: `bash infra/hosted/check.sh` exited 0 on the Mac mini (linux/arm64), 11 passed, 0 failed: `agree_test` (32 passed, among them every refuses case of the moved lock rules), `it_refuses_the_real_project`, `a_release_brings_the_stack_up`, `the_stack_builds_and_every_service_answers`, `the_design_files_and_the_gallery_are_served`, `nothing_but_the_proxy_is_published`, `no_container_runs_as_root`, `the_acceptance_suite_passes_against_the_containers` (278 passed, 1 deselected), `backup_test` (12 passed), the new `it_saves_the_logs_of_a_failed_run`, and `it_leaves_nothing_behind`. It ran at 4d13a17's tree; 681a250 changes only docs and the skill, none of them copied into an image.

Acceptance tests, failing before the change:

```
$ bash scripts/ci/changed-areas.test.sh
FAIL infra/hosted/x sets hosted
     expected: hosted=true
     got:      hosted=
FAIL Core/src/x.rs does not set hosted
     expected: hosted=false
     got:      hosted=
...
62 passed, 40 failed

$ bash scripts/ci/workflows-locked.test.sh
FAIL Dockerfiles install locked
     got:      bash: .../scripts/ci/dockerfile.sh: No such file or directory
FAIL sample Dockerfile lines
11 passed, 2 failed

$ bash scripts/ci/ci-ok.test.sh      # with the hosted job in ci.yml, before ci-ok needed it
FAIL ci-ok needs every other job in ci.yml
     jobs:  brain canary changes core dotnet e2e hosted libs scripts web
     needs: brain canary changes core dotnet e2e libs scripts web
11 passed, 1 failed
```

The two `ci-ok.test.sh` Acceptance cases for a failed and a skipped `hosted` job passed from the start, since `ci-ok.sh` judges any job generically; the needs check above is what went red.

and passing after it:

```
$ bash scripts/ci/changed-areas.test.sh
102 passed, 0 failed
$ bash scripts/ci/workflows-locked.test.sh
13 passed, 0 failed
$ bash scripts/ci/ci-ok.test.sh
12 passed, 0 failed
```

The last criterion, the `hosted` job on GitHub's runner (linux/amd64), passed at 681a250: `gh pr checks 267` shows `hosted / check pass 11m24s` and `ci-ok pass`, with every other job passing, and its log (`gh run view 43689982944 --job 132738434055 --log`) shows `check.sh` at 11 passed, 0 failed, the same eleven cases as the Mac mini run, its suite at 278 passed, 1 deselected, and the backup tests at 12 passed, 0 failed.

Screenshots, desktop and 390px phone width:

No UI change.

Not verified: the upload of `hosted-logs` on a failure is not exercised on GitHub unless the job fails; `check.sh` writing the directory is proven by `it_saves_the_logs_of_a_failed_run`.

## Doc changes

- `infra/hosted/README.md`: the intro says CI runs `check.sh`; "check.sh" lists `design/ui`'s packages among its prerequisites, the new case, and `HOSTED_CHECK_LOGS`; the lock rule names `scripts/ci/dockerfile.sh`; a new "In CI" section says when CI runs the check, what it leaves to a release, what the job installs, and the amd64 and arm64 split. "Neither runs in CI yet" is gone.
- `infra/README.md`: the paragraph on what a new service needs gains its Dockerfile and entries in `infra/hosted/`, which `agree.test.sh` holds it to.
- `High-level/docs/platform-architecture.md`, "What it costs, and how it is paid": names the `hosted` job among those `ci-ok` judges.
- `.claude/skills/pick-up-slice/SKILL.md`, step 9: the **hosted** entry, after e2e. Named by the slice's Tasks.
- `docs/README.md`'s line for `scripts/ci/` is unchanged, as Settled says.

## Waits for the owner

The slice's Risk is high, the branch touches `.github/`, `scripts/` and `.claude/`, and it carries `has-decision`. The merge gate will not merge this pull request; the owner reviews and merges it, once the reviewer has approved it and the runner has given it `owner-merge` or `owner-decision`. The decision that waits for him:

- `hosted.yml` installs Node 26 and `design/ui`'s packages, for the suite's `axe-core`, against Settled's "installs no Node".

Merging confirms it, and a comment changes it.

labels.name: owner-decision
labels.description: A decision the agent made waits for the owner's answer

labels.name: has-decision
labels.description: The implementer flagged a decision. Read by the gate and the runner, not a signal to the owner
